changes: p2 (Vājabahādura): role changed from 'king' to 'other'. He is named in the author's verse about when the text was composed, not as the king reigning when this copy was made in saṃvat 1844. Confidence lowered to medium because the verse is corrupt.
Kept the relation p1 under_reign_of p2, but it describes when the text was composed, not when it was copied.
Date: kept VS 1844 = c. 1787 CE. The colophon says only 'saṃvat', so the era is assumed; this is now stated in the notes.
Notes: added a reading of the Śāka chronogram in the verse and how it may relate to the catalogue's 'SAM 1695'.

notes: The opening verse is the author's statement of when the text was composed, not a statement about this copy. It reads 'śāke vā saptatithibhir bhūye vājabahādure', probably for '... bhūpe Bājabahādure' ('when Bājabahādura was king'). This is probably Baz Bahadur Chand of Kumaon (r. c. 1638–1678), so he is recorded with the role 'other', not as the reigning king of this copy. The Śāka chronogram is corrupt. One possible reading, right to left: 'vā' as a garbled word for 5 (bāṇa?), sapta = 7, tithi = 15, giving Śāka 1575 = c. 1653 CE. This is not certain. The copy date 'saṃvat 1844' gives no era; VS is assumed (c. 1787 CE). The catalogue's 'SAM 1695' (VS 1695 = c. 1638 CE) does not appear in the quoted colophon. It may come from the cataloguer's reading of the composition verse, and it conflicts with the copy date saṃvat 1844. The catalogue's place, Vārāṇasī, also does not appear in the colophon. No scribe or owner is named.
